Ba_Step1: 1. SCSKiller deletes this game's shader caches ({1} the game's own) and starts the game. Load a save you can load again and play. The {0} minutes count from the game's first frame, loading and pauses included.
Ba_Step2: 2. Close the game. SCSKiller deletes the caches again and compiles the game's shaders.
Ba_Step3: 3. Load the same save and play the same {0} minutes.
Ba_Step4: 4. You get a before and after report you can save and share.
Ba_Warning: This also deletes the game's own shader cache, which isn't backed up and can be 2 GB. The game rebuilds it, which can take minutes.

Settings_ActiveCheckDesc: Helps us count active installs so we can size our servers. Once a day, the app's version and GPU vendor, no identifier.
Settings_AllowAntiCheatDesc: Some games contain anti-cheat that can ban accounts using the recorder. Turn this on to enable it per game, at your own risk. SCSKiller isn't responsible for bans.
Settings_AllowAntiCheatRecorder: Allow the recorder in games with anti-cheat (at your own risk)
Settings_AntiCheatBody:
For one session, SCSKiller puts its recorder (a d3d12.dll) next to the game's exe.

Games with anti-cheat can treat the recorder as cheating and ban your account, during the session or later. No game is known to be safe.

SCSKiller removes every file it places when the game exits, or after a crash at your next logon.

Enabling the recorder in these games is at your own risk. SCSKiller isn't responsible for bans.
Settings_AntiCheatDetails: Details on recording in games with anti-cheat

Settings_AutoShaderDesc: A beta feature of the NVIDIA App: after a driver update it re-compiles the games you have already played. SCSKiller adds everything else, so both together are best. The overlap costs little: shaders NVIDIA already rebuilt take about 1 ms each here.

Settings_SetLimitBody:
This is a global {0} driver setting: it applies to every game on this PC, not only the ones SCSKiller compiles, and stays until you change it. Windows will ask for administrator permission.

Raising it deletes nothing. Lowering it below what is used now makes the driver delete older entries, and those games stutter again. You can switch back to the driver default here at any time.
